_help: THE ONLY FILE YOU EDIT TO ANNOUNCE A FEATURE. The guided tour is built from it.
First start: the whole list is the tour. After an update: the island compares this file with the copy the user saw last
(~/.local/state/island/features.seen.json) and shows only entries that are new, or whose "rev" went up.
So: add an entry at the place you want it in the order. Fixed a typo? Leave rev. Changed what it does? rev + 1.
Fields: id (unique, never reuse) | title | body | rev (default 1) | quick: true = in the Quick tour
try: { check: launcher|media|perf|notifs|term|cheat|tree|notes|screenshot|clipboard, say: "what to do" } = a challenge: the step waits until you do it (shell.qml tourCheck), +1 star
target: bar | perf | media | corner | notifs | term   (the dark screen leaves a hole there; the hole follows the real size)
demo:   launcher | perf | media | corner | notifs | term | cheat | cmds | tree | settings | calendar   (opened for the step, closed after)
keys: ["SUPER", "TAB"] shown as key caps | only: "sysmode" = skip when sysmode is not installed
core: true = existing users who update to the first tour-enabled version are assumed to know it (they only see non-core entries)
A demo that fills the screen (cheat, cmds, tree, settings, calendar) shows the card at the bottom without dimming.

features.title: Welcome to Halcyon
features.body: A quick look around, about a minute. The screen goes dim except for the part we are talking about, and you can poke at it. Esc skips the tour at any time; replay it with >tour.

features.title: A calmer look
features.body: Halcyon has a new interface: flat frosted panes with one quiet outline, softer buttons without borders, rounder corners, more room, and the moving stars kept but softer. Prefer the earlier look? Settings > Appearance > Look > Interface: Legacy brings it back, and New returns to this one.

features.title: The island
features.body: Workspaces, the clock, music bars and your Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and battery in one pill. It changes size with what it shows, and so does the spotlight. Click a number to change workspace; scroll over it to move through them.

try.say: Tap the Super key on its own (the one with the Windows logo).

features.title: One search bar for everything
features.body: Tap SUPER and the bar grows into a search box. Type to find an app, press . to list all of them, > for commands (wallpaper, settings, power mode, this tour) and = for a calculator.

features.title: Performance page
features.body: Drag the bar to the left, or scroll or two-finger swipe over it: CPU, RAM, temperature and GPU, plus your hardware and the active power mode. The GPU is never woken up just to be measured.

features.title: Media page
features.body: Drag the bar to the right for whatever is playing: cover, track, play / pause and a seek bar. Works with any player that speaks MPRIS. The Lyrics chip next to the artist opens the lyrics of whatever plays (any player; no account needed), the Queue chip shows what plays next on Spotify (needs spotify_player).

features.title: Quick settings
features.body: Touch the bottom-right corner for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound, brightness, power mode, Focus mode and the power buttons. Click a Wi-Fi or Bluetooth chip to pick a network or device; right-click it to switch the radio off.

try.say: Open the notification centre: Super + Shift + N.

features.title: Notifications
features.body: There is no bell: touch the right edge of the screen and the notification centre slides out. Swipe a notification sideways to dismiss it. SUPER + SHIFT + D toggles Do not disturb.

try.say: Pop the console out: Super + Shift + Enter.

features.title: Console
features.body: Touch the top-left corner for a small console: run a one-off command without opening a terminal. Tab completes, Esc closes, help lists what works. When a command asks something ("Proceed? [y/N]" or a sudo password) you answer right in its input line, and Ctrl+C stops it with everything it started.

features.title: Shortcuts: tree or pages
features.body: Every keybind and gesture, searchable. Click any shortcut to change it, or add your own at the bottom. Like Settings it has two views: the branching tree, or Pages with a menu of groups on the left; switch with the chip in its header. Nothing to memorise.

features.title: Sysmode commands
features.body: Every sysmode console command as a tree, same look as the shortcuts. Click one and it is put in the console; you press Enter to run it.

try.say: Open the tree view: Super + Tab.

features.title: Tree view
features.body: Your laptop, workspaces and windows as living branches. Click a node to jump there, or drag a window onto another workspace to move it.

features.title: Settings
features.body: Type >settings in the search bar: theme, bar style, transparency, motion, gestures, default apps and more. >bar builder lets you drag your own bar together and >widget builder designs your desktop widgets.

features.title: Desktop widgets
features.body: Clocks, system usage, now playing, an audio visualizer, weather, notes, a Focus timer with a day streak and more, drawn right on your desktop. Type >widget builder to pick a layout and a look for each one.

features.title: Place widgets with the mouse
features.body: Type >place widgets on the desktop, then drag a widget where you want it (it snaps to the middle and the edges), resize it with the corner dot or the mouse wheel, and add or remove widgets on the spot. Esc when you are done.

features.title: Desktop builder
features.body: A picture of your desktop: where every widget sits, a switch for the top bar, and the screen corner that opens each box. Drag widgets in the picture, or onto a corner. Type >desktop builder.

features.title: Top bar on or off
features.body: Prefer a clean desktop? Type >top bar on / off to hide the bar and use widgets instead. The launcher, the pages and every box still open from the top edge.

features.title: Google Calendar
features.body: Type >calendar: your events by day, what is next, and a notification before each one starts, on top of everything. Press one button, copy the secret iCal address in your browser, and it connects by itself; it is read-only.

features.title: Notification box builder
features.body: Arrange the notification box: place it in any corner (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) or along the screen edge, switch between edge strip or corner activation triggers, tune width, constellations and padding. Type >notification box builder.

try.say: Open the new-note panel: Super + N.

features.title: Notes, tasks and reminders
features.body: SUPER + N opens a small panel on the side: type, press Enter, saved. >all notes lists everything with search, pin, tick off and a Tasks filter. The Notes widget on the desktop has an Add a note row that opens the same panel. Turn on Settings > Notes > Sort new notes into tasks and your local Ollama model decides whether a note is a task ("call mom at 6" gets a time and a reminder notification, "idea: dark lock screen" stays a note); the model's short comment shows right under the note in All notes (Think asks again), and a note that says "later" gets a few gentle nudges during the day (Remind > Later today, every 3 hours by default, never at night); it is off by default and a note is always saved first. The stars in the panels drift like your desktop stars and follow the Desktop builder's direction, speed and colour.

features.title: Choose your terminal logo
features.body: Settings > Terminal greeting: Adaptive, Arch, BlackArch, Kali, your own ASCII art, or no logo at all.

features.title: Display & Projector Manager
features.body: Press SUPER + P or type >display or >projector: clone screen to a projector/TV, extend right/left for multi-monitors, or switch to external-only for presentations. Themed with Halcyon glass and moving stars.

features.title: Local AI Assistant & System Diagnostics
features.body: Type 'ai' or 'advisor' in any terminal: an intelligent local AI that diagnoses system health, checks memory pressure, inspects logs, answers questions, and asks for your confirmation before making any system changes. Recommends the best local models for your hardware.

features.title: Background Apps & Themed Badges
features.body: Apps running in the tray appear in a clean, compact glass box. Themed status badges highlight active background apps and unread notifications with smooth animations.

features.title: Touchpad Gestures & Workspaces
features.body: Smooth 1:1 workspace finger tracking with calibrated sensitivity so workspaces switch smoothly when you want them to, without accidental triggers.

features.title: Move between windows
features.body: SUPER + the arrow keys move focus to the window next to you. In the scrolling (niri) layout (SUPER + ALT + T) left and right walk the columns and the view follows, so you can always get back to what you opened before; up and down move inside a column. Add SHIFT to move the window itself.

features.title: One thing plays at a time
features.body: Start a YouTube video while Spotify plays and the music pauses; when the video stops or ends, the music carries on by itself. If you paused the music yourself it stays paused, and it works with any player on the media bus (browser tabs, mpv, VLC ...). In Settings > Startup & background you can switch it off, choose whether the music comes back afterwards, and how many seconds (1, 2, 5 or 10) to wait before it does.

features.title: Safety check clock
features.body: Settings > Backup & safety now shows how many days since your last scan and how many are left until the next one (automatic scan or reminder), and says when a scan is running right now.

features.title: Memory graph and Health
features.body: Startup & processes > Health draws the memory of all of Halcyon together over the last ten minutes, and lists the parts that grew most since the window opened, so a spike can be matched to its cause. Hover the small ? next to a word to see what it means. Settings > Performance has the RAM and CPU limits it measures against; it only advises, it never stops anything.

features.title: Timelines
features.body: The timeline from Backup & safety now also shows when your wallpaper last changed (top of Settings > Wallpaper), when the system last really updated (Settings > Backup & safety) and your Focus streak against your best (Settings > Focus mode). They only read what is already there.

features.title: Profiles
features.body: Settings > Performance > Profiles & safe mode: Work, Gaming, Battery or Night sets stars, blur, island motion, brightness and the top bar in one switch. The first time you leave Custom your own values are saved, and Custom brings them back. In a terminal: halcyon profile battery.

features.title: Safe mode
features.body: If a tweak makes the island hard to use, SUPER + ALT + F12 (or halcyon safe-mode, which also works from a TTY) turns off blur, shadows, animations, stars and motion and reloads. The same key, or halcyon safe-mode back, puts your values back exactly.

features.title: Blurred wallpaper on the lock screen
features.body: Settings > Power & lock > Lock screen background > Blurred wallpaper shows your wallpaper behind the clock, with Blur and Tint sliders (tint 0 % = the wallpaper as it is). It is only loaded while locked, falls back to the plain colour if the picture cannot be read, and never touches the password box.

features.title: Clipboard history
features.body: Type >clipboard in the launcher: what you copied lately, with search. Click a line or press Enter and it is on the clipboard again. Pictures show a preview, colours a swatch and links their site; Tab filters text, links or pictures. Copies from password managers are never kept, and Clear history empties it. The history is the one that was already there (Settings > Startup & background), no extra process.

try.say: Open the screenshot panel: Super + Ctrl + S.

features.title: Screenshot panel
features.body: A small panel: Region, Window or Full screen, then Copy, Save or Both. Also >screenshot. SUPER + SHIFT + S still drags a region at once, as before.

features.title: Lyrics and queue
features.body: On the music page (hover the music in the bar) there are two new chips next to the artist: Lyrics and Queue. They open a panel with the lyrics of what plays and what plays next. Lyrics need nothing installed: Halcyon asks a free lyrics site (lrclib.net, then lyrics.ovh) or reads a .lrc file next to a local song, and uses spotify_player too when you have it (choose the source with halcyon-music.py source). The queue is Spotify's and needs spotify_player. Also >lyrics and >queue. The queue is read-only.

features.title: Login splash
features.body: A short animation of moving stars and the Halcyon sparkle now plays when you log in (about 3.5 seconds; a click or any key skips it). See it any time with >splash, or turn it off in Settings > Power & lock.

features.title: Splash everywhere, weekly sky, time of day
features.body: The splash now also plays when you unlock (the stars rush out again) and when you shut down or restart (they are drawn back in). >weekly sky draws your week as stars: one for every focus session, task you ticked off and calendar event, with a Save picture button to share it. Settings > Splash, sky & time of day also has a wallpaper wash that follows the sun, and optional soft sounds.

features.title: Your local AI, around the desktop
features.body: Ask it how to change Halcyon: >ask how do I turn off the constellations gives the steps from your real Settings, and Enter takes you there. Other questions get a quick answer, and >do turns plain English into an action ("move this window to workspace 3", "gaming mode on"). The clipboard history can summarise or rewrite an entry (the sparkle on a row), the lyrics panel explains the song, Notes > Organise suggests tags, groups and merges duplicates, and a Daily brief sums up your day each morning. Failed services and island errors get explained in a notification. All of it runs on your own model and stops with Settings > AI features. The Desktop builder also has a Lock screen side now.

features.title: Your focus streak, up close
features.body: >focus streak graph opens your streak with a flame that flickers, today's minutes against the goal, the last two weeks and twelve weeks of focus, and milestones that light up. Space starts a Focus session right there. Every widget can now go on the lock screen too.

features.title: Game Center
features.body: >gamecenter opens your games: Steam and Flatpak games are found by Refresh, and Add game browses for a Windows .exe. Each game has a For your PC card: your computer's class (A to D), the settings that run it well and which Proton to install, applied in one click. After Play it tells you what is happening, and if a game quits early it says why. The star on a cover (or Ctrl+F on a >game row in the launcher) makes a game a favourite: favourites come first, here and in >game.

features.title: Study Center
features.body: >study opens it. Add lecture slides, PDFs (scanned ones too), Word or PowerPoint files, notes or a photo of a page, then ask about them in plain words: the answer comes only from your files and names the page, and a click on the page opens it there. Summary, Quiz and Flashcards turn them into revision material; a page range does one chapter. Everything stays on this computer.

features.title: Everyday tools on a key
features.body: Super + Shift + C picks a colour on screen and copies it. Super + Alt + M measures a box, Super + Alt + Z zooms, Super + Alt + V types a saved snippet, Alt + Shift + Tab lists your windows. >wifi qr shows a code friends scan to join your Wi-Fi. All of them are in the launcher too (type > and the name).

features.title: Everything, in one place
features.body: Settings opens on Discover: every feature in one list, the new ones marked, with the guided tour one click away.

features.title: That's it
features.body: Everything follows your wallpaper colours, so try >wallpaper gallery next. Replay this tour any time with >tour.
